commentary:
Energy is again the epicenter this morning: Brent is up 1.7% to $104.83 and WTI +1.25% to $93.31 after an Iranian official warned the war with the US could expand into the Indian Ocean, dimming hopes for a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The crude curve is screaming physical tightness — Brent's prompt spread near $5 backwardated, the WTI cash roll at a record, and WTI's 50/100-day golden cross confirming momentum. That oil impulse is feeding straight into the bond market, where the selloff deepened and the US 30-year yield hit its highest since 2004.

With the Fed having delivered its first hike in three years and markets increasingly convinced more work is needed, oil-driven inflation is colliding with heavy fiscal and AI-related financing demand — a competition for capital that should keep long-end yields under pressure. Jobless claims at 197k, below estimates, gave the Fed no reason to relent. The transmission is a classic bear-steepener: long bond and Ultra futures down, Bund and Buxl following, while the short end held. Equity-index futures are lower across the board — Nasdaq -0.9% as long-duration tech absorbs the rate shock — despite a constructive Trump-Xi summit that extended the trade truce to January 10 with AI talks confirmed, lifting KOSPI futures +1.4%.

The dollar hit a fresh two-month peak, pressing gold (-0.4%) and silver (-1.3%) even as risk sours — real-yield and dollar headwinds trumping haven demand, while copper firmed on the truce. TTF gas jumped 3.4% on the same supply anxiety. Watch Hormuz headlines, summit deliverables, and whether the long end finds a bid.
